quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will still be in your system.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles are entering the road.
Traffic signal ahead.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagon signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Make sure your motorcycle is in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that comes on when the ignition is on and the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often ride to the left or right of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: Within minutes of
About an hour after
About two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects your riding ability within minutes of drinking. Driving any vehicle under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have room to maneuver.
You have fewer escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have fewer escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control sign.
Move to the outer edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you easiest.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that puts you in other drivers' view as soon as possible when approaching a blind intersection.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Traction is poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line first, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line first, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or stop sign, stop first where indicated. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before entering the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when they are riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, the center lane position is best for a motorcyclist following a car. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if needed.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: The greatest chance of a conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles happens at intersections.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure right away. Then re-apply the brake gently with controlled pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Darkly-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even during the day. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When someone passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right side is dangerous. It may cause the passing driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: When turning, when should you change gears?

options.text: Change gears before the turn.
Change gears during the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep going through it.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Drink caffeine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine and other stimulants can make fatigue worse when they wear off. Bad weather like wind, rain, and snow also causes fatigue. Dress warmly and use a windshield for long-distance rides.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.
